paragraphs.text: # dsh-rea-toggle
English · 中文

One switch per conversation that decides whether the **REA**
(`reverse-engineer-anything`) MCP serve
r's context reaches the model at all.

REA registers **207 tool schemas** plus a multi-kilobyte server-instructions
block. `dsh-mcp-client`

puts both on the **global** layer, so every agent pays
for them on every request — whether or not t

he turn has anything to do with
reverse engineering.
With this plugin installed, a small pill appears below the composer:

- **REA on** (green) — exactly the pre-install behaviour. REA's tools and
instructions are visible t

o the model.
- **REA off** (grey) — those 207 tool schemas and the `mcp:rea` instructions
block **le
ave the model context**, taking effect on the next step.

**The switch is per conversation.** Each conversation remembers its own
position, and a new conversa

tion starts **off**. That is the whole point: a
conversation about a web app should not pay for 207

reverse-engineering schemas
just because some other conversation needs them. Subagents inherit the p

osition
of the conversation that created them, so delegating inside reverse-engineering
work does no
t silently break the subagent.

The same switch is on the keyboard: `/rea off`, `/rea on`, `/rea status`,
`/rea toggle` — all acting
on the conversation you typed them in.

Nothing is uninstalled and nothing restarts. The MCP connection stays up; the
model simply stops bei
ng told those tools exist.
## English
### What it actually does

The token cost comes from two different places that travel two different paths,
so one mechanism is

ost comes from two different places that travel two different paths,
so one mechanism is not enough:
| Target | Mechanism |
| Tool schemas | `tools.restrict({ deny })` is called **in each agent's own context**. `ToolRuntime.
view()` filters what that scope *inherits* from the global layer, and the model-facing schema list i
s rebuilt from that view on every assembly. The reserved `run_code` transport sits outside the filte

rable layers, so it is unaffected. |
| Instructions text | `dsh-mcp-client` registers the server ins
tructions as a prompt section named `mcp:<server>` at order `MCP_SERVERS` (3100). **A scoped section
with the same name shadows the global one** — a documented contract of `systemPrompt.section()` ("a
scoped section shadows a global section with the same name"), not an implementation detail — and an
empty section is dropped at render (`renderPrompt` keeps only `text.length > 0`). Registering that
name and returning `''` therefore removes the block for that agent alone. |

Both are scoped registrations, so disposing them restores the previous state
exactly. That is why fl
ipping the switch needs no restart and no reload.

Coverage includes **subagents**: `agent/created` is serial and awaited by the
registry, so installin
g inside it lands ahead of any prompt assembly.
### Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Or point at a checkout:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The bundle row id is `rea-toggle`; the package name is `dsh-rea-toggle`.
### Use
| Where | What |
| Pill under the composer | Click to flip **this conversation**. Green = on, grey = off, red border

= the host did not answer. |
| `/rea off` · `/rea on` | Set this conversation's position. `enable` /

`disable` work too. |
| `/rea toggle` | Flip this conversation. |
| `/rea status` | Report this con
versation's position. |

A new conversation starts off. The first time you turn one on, that conversation
is remembered; conv

ersations you never touch stay on the default and are not
written down.

Positions are remembered in `$DSH_HOME/rea-toggle.json` (usually
`~/.dsh/rea-toggle.json`), keyed by

session id, and survive a restart. The file
keeps the 500 most recently changed conversations; an o

lder one simply falls
back to the default.
### Configuration
Every field is optional.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Changing `server` governs a different MCP server by the same rules: tool prefix
`mcp__<server>__`, i

nstructions section `mcp:<server>`. Because the mechanism is
generic, this works for any MCP server

whose tools are bridged by
`dsh-mcp-client` — the REA case is just the one that motivated it.

`defaultEnabled` exists for anyone who wants the pre-plugin behaviour back: with
it on, a conversati

on nobody has switched behaves exactly as if this plugin were
not installed.
### HTTP API

The Client half talks to the Host over one exact route on the bare `webServer`
(the same shape other

bundles use, so it does not travel through the `/api`
prefix fence). The conversation is `session=`

on GET and a body field on POST:
the pill always knows which conversation it is showing, and a requ

est that does
not say cannot be answered for it.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`known` says whether this conversation has ever been switched; when it is
`false`, `enabled` is just

`defaultEnabled` and nothing has been written yet.
`agents` is how many live agents of that convers

ation are currently covered;
`tools` is how many of the governed server's tools were recognised, whi

ch is the
honest answer to "did it find REA at all" — if it reads `0`, the server is not
connected u

nder that name (and stays `0`-safe because `restrictableNames` is the
denyable set, not the filtered

at name (and stays `0`-safe because `restrictableNames` is the
denyable set, not the filtered view).
### Scope and limits

- **One server per row by default.** Other MCP servers are untouched; use
`servers` to govern more t

han one.
- **Hidden, not unloaded.** The MCP connection stays up and the REA process
keeps running.

When the switch is off the model simply cannot reach it —
including indirectly through `run_code`. T

hat is deliberate: leaving a second
path open would save only half the tokens.
- **Per-conversation

state, in-process.** Positions are read from the file at
`apply()` and written on every change. Two

DSH instances sharing one profile
each read it once and do not live-sync with each other.
- **It doe

s not delete anything.** Turning it off is reversible in one click,
and uninstalling the bundle lift
s every registration.
### Verify it yourself

The claim is that the tools are gone from the model's context, not merely
hidden in a UI. Check it w
here the model's own view is exposed:
